formation.title: The Unification of Germany
formation.text:
The dream of centuries has been realized. From the fractured mosaic of principalities, free cities, and kingdoms, a single German state has emerged, an empire that speaks with one voice and commands the respect of all Europe. The question now is not whether Germany will be great, but what kind of greatness it will pursue. Will this new empire be built on the strength of its armies, its drill fields echoing with the cadence that once shook the continent? Or will it be the triumph of industry and commerce, the Zollverein's vision fulfilled, a nation bound by rail, trade, and the relentless march of progress?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Through blood and iron shall Germany endure.

modifiers.name: Blood and Iron
modifiers.text: The German nation was forged not through speeches and majority votes, but through iron and blood. Our armies march with unshakeable discipline, and our forges burn day and night to arm the mightiest military force in Europe.

options.text: Commerce and industry shall be our foundation.

modifiers.name: Legacy of the Zollverein
modifiers.text: Before there was a German state, there was a German market. The customs union that bound the German lands economically now fuels an empire of industry, scholarship, and diplomatic influence that shapes the continent.

advances.name: Guild Heritage
advances.text: The elaborate system of craft guilds that governed German towns established standards of quality, protected artisans, and created the civic institutions that would define German urban life for centuries.

advances.name: Mining Tradition
advances.text: The silver mines of the Harz Mountains and the Erzgebirge fueled German commerce and attracted miners, engineers, and metallurgists whose expertise transformed the region into Europe's mining heartland.

advances.name: Reichstag Tradition
advances.text: The Imperial Diet, gathering princes, bishops, and free city representatives, established a tradition of negotiation and compromise that shaped German political culture.

advances.name: Hanseatic Roots
advances.text: The Hanseatic League connected German merchants from Lubeck to Novgorod, establishing trading posts and commercial networks that dominated Northern European trade for centuries.

advances.name: Minnesang Tradition
advances.text: The courtly love poetry of the Minnesanger, Walther von der Vogelweide, Wolfram von Eschenbach, and their peers, established a German literary tradition that rivaled the troubadours of France.

advances.name: Gutenberg Press
advances.text: Johannes Gutenberg's movable-type printing press, developed in Mainz around 1440, launched a revolution in the dissemination of knowledge that reshaped European civilization.

event.title: The Gutenberg Revolution
event.text: Johannes Gutenberg's invention of the movable-type printing press in Mainz around 1440 has unleashed a revolution more profound than any battle. What once took a monk years to copy by hand can now be produced in hundreds of copies within weeks. Ideas spread like wildfire across the German lands and beyond, scholarly works, religious texts, political pamphlets, and scientific treatises pour from the presses of Mainz, Strasbourg, Nuremberg, and Augsburg. The monopoly on knowledge held by the Church and the elite is broken forever. Germany stands at the center of this transformation, its printers shaping the intellectual life of an entire continent.

options.text: The press shall be the sword of the mind.

advances.name: University Tradition
advances.text: The founding of universities at Heidelberg, Leipzig, Cologne, and Erfurt created centers of learning that attracted scholars from across Europe and laid the groundwork for German intellectual leadership.

advances.name: Imperial Banking
advances.text:
The Fugger and Welser banking houses of Augsburg financed emperors, popes, and colonial ventures, making southern Germany the financial capital of Europe in the Renaissance era. Their fortune was smelted before it was lent: at the Saiger works silver was parted from copper ore with lead, and the Fuggers held the trade in both metals.

Available in: Bergwerk

advances.name: Civic Autonomy
advances.text:
The tradition of self-governing free imperial cities (Nuremberg, Augsburg, Hamburg, Frankfurt) created spaces of burgher independence, commercial innovation, and civic pride unique to the German political landscape. A free city brewed and sold drink by its own right, and the cellar under the town hall paid for the hall.

Available in: Rathaus

advances.name: Meistersinger Guilds
advances.text: The Meistersinger guilds of Nuremberg, Augsburg, and other German cities organized the art of song into a disciplined craft, preserving and advancing German cultural traditions through competitive composition.

advances.name: Reformation Crucible
advances.text:
The Protestant Reformation, ignited by Martin Luther's challenge to papal authority in 1517, was born on German soil and forever transformed the relationship between faith, politics, and individual conscience in the Western world. Its weapon was the press: cheap pamphlets, the Flugschriften, carried the quarrel into every market town.

Available in: Druckerei

event.title: The Reformation
event.text: The nailing of ninety-five theses to a church door in Wittenberg has shaken the foundations of Christendom. Martin Luther's challenge to papal authority, amplified by the printing presses that are themselves a German invention, has ignited a confessional revolution that divides the German lands between old faith and new. Princes choose sides not merely out of conviction but calculation, the Reformation offers freedom from Roman taxation and the assertion of territorial sovereignty. How shall Germany navigate this upheaval?

options.text: Stand firm in our confession, one faith, one people.

modifiers.name: Confessional Conviction
modifiers.text: Germany stands united in faith, drawing strength from its religious identity to build a more cohesive society.

options.text: Cuius regio, eius religio. Pragmatism preserves the peace.

modifiers.name: Cuius Regio, Eius Religio
modifiers.text: The pragmatic acceptance of confessional diversity has brought stability to the German lands, allowing commerce and diplomacy to flourish where religious war once threatened.

advances.name: Arms Manufacture
advances.text: German armorers and weaponsmiths, particularly in centers like Nuremberg, Augsburg, and Solingen, produced some of the finest weapons and armor in Europe, supplying armies and princes across the continent.

advances.name: Schwarze Reiter Tradition
advances.text: The Black Riders revolutionized cavalry warfare by making the pistol their primary weapon, employing the caracole formation to deliver devastating volleys before charging home with sword in hand.

advances.name: German Silver Rush
advances.text:
The exploitation of rich silver deposits in the Erzgebirge and Harz Mountains created a torrent of precious metal that funded German princes, powered the mint cities, and attracted mining expertise from across Europe.

Available in: Bergwerk

advances.name: Territorial Administration
advances.text: The development of professional territorial bureaucracies in the German states, with trained officials, systematic record-keeping, and codified law, created some of the most effective administrations in early modern Europe.

advances.name: Westphalian Order
advances.text: The Peace of Westphalia in 1648 ended the Thirty Years' War and established the foundational principles of modern international relations: state sovereignty, non-interference, and the balance of power.

event.title: The Peace of Westphalia
event.text: After thirty years of the most devastating war Europe has ever known, a war that killed perhaps a third of the German population, the exhausted powers have gathered at Osnabruck and Munster to forge a new order. The treaties of Westphalia establish principles that will reshape the world: the sovereignty of states, the right of rulers to determine the religion of their territory, and the balance of power as the foundation of international relations. Germany emerges scarred but with a new framework for coexistence.

options.text: Sovereignty is sacred. No power shall dictate to another.

modifiers.name: Westphalian Sovereignty
modifiers.text: The principle of state sovereignty, born from the ashes of the Thirty Years' War, grants Germany diplomatic authority and internal cohesion that its rivals envy.

options.text: Balance and diplomacy shall prevent the next catastrophe.

modifiers.name: Westphalian Balance
modifiers.text: Germany has embraced the role of arbiter in European affairs, leveraging its central position and diplomatic expertise to maintain the balance of power.

advances.name: Confessional State
advances.text: The integration of religious authority into state governance, whether Protestant or Catholic, created a distinctive German model of confessional politics that shaped society, education, and culture for centuries.

advances.name: Military Drill Tradition
advances.text: The systematic drill innovations pioneered by Leopold of Anhalt-Dessau, the iron ramrod, the lockstep march, and standardized loading procedures, transformed German infantry into the most disciplined soldiers in Europe.

advances.name: Solingen Forges
advances.text:
The blade-smiths of Solingen and the gunsmiths of Suhl produced weapons of legendary quality, making Germany the armory of Europe and establishing an industrial tradition that endures to this day.

Available in: Waffenschmiede

advances.name: Cameralist Administration
advances.text: Cameralism, the German science of state finance and administration, trained generations of officials in systematic revenue collection, economic management, and the rational organization of the state.

advances.name: Schützen Companies
advances.text: Every German town kept a shooting guild, and its best shots carried rifled pieces of their own. The states drew picked marksmen from them, the Schützen, who fought in open order ahead of the line as skirmishers and sharpshooters.

advances.name: Deutsche Feldartillerie
advances.text: German artillery schools, building on centuries of metallurgical expertise, produced field guns of exceptional range and accuracy that would prove decisive on the battlefields of Europe.

advances.name: Aufklarung
advances.text: The German Enlightenment, the Aufklarung, produced Kant, Lessing, and Goethe, and championed reason, education, and the reform of governance. Its impact on German universities, administration, and culture was transformative.

advances.name: Prussian Bureaucratic Model
advances.text: The Prussian civil service, with its rigorous examinations, systematic training, and incorruptible efficiency, became the model for modern bureaucracy that states across Europe sought to emulate.

advances.name: Standing Army Doctrine
advances.text: The transition from unreliable mercenary bands to permanent, professionally trained standing armies gave German states the military foundation for sustained campaigns and effective defense. In Prussia the canton regulation of 1733 gave every regiment a district of its own, whose enrolled men drilled with it each spring and went home to the plough.

advances.name: Landwehr System
advances.text: The Landwehr, established during the Wars of Liberation against Napoleon, created a citizen-militia that combined patriotic fervor with military training, vastly expanding the available manpower of the German state.

advances.name: Zollverein
advances.text: The German Customs Union, the Zollverein, eliminated hundreds of internal tariff barriers and created a unified economic space that made German unification not just conceivable but inevitable.

event.title: The Zollverein
event.text: The German Customs Union, the Zollverein, has achieved through commerce what diplomacy and war could not, the practical unification of the German lands. Beginning with Prussia's customs reforms and gradually absorbing state after state, the Zollverein has demolished hundreds of internal tariff barriers, created a unified market of millions, and laid the iron rails that bind the German economy into a single engine of production. Factories rise along the Rhine and Ruhr, merchants trade freely from Hamburg to Munich, and the old mosaic of petty toll stations gives way to the modern economy.

options.text: Integration through trade. Let the customs union deepen.

modifiers.name: Customs Integration
modifiers.text: The dismantling of internal tariff barriers has created a vast unified market, spurring trade and prosperity across the German lands.

options.text: Invest in industry. The factories shall be our strength.

modifiers.name: Industrial Investment
modifiers.text: Massive investment in factories, railways, and infrastructure has transformed Germany into an industrial powerhouse.

advances.name: German Industrialization
advances.text:
The transformation of the Rhineland, Ruhr, and Silesia into industrial powerhouses, with coal mines, steel mills, and railway networks, propelled Germany from an agricultural patchwork into a modern industrial economy.

Available in: Bergwerk

advances.name: Humboldtian Education
advances.text: Wilhelm von Humboldt's university reform, uniting research and teaching, emphasizing academic freedom, and valuing Bildung over mere vocational training, created the modern research university model adopted worldwide.

advances.name: Realpolitik
advances.text: The pragmatic, interest-driven approach to foreign policy associated with Bismarck, where diplomacy served power, alliances were tools, and idealism yielded to calculated advantage, reshaped European politics.

destiny.name: The German Question
destiny.text: Germany has been unified, but the question of what Germany shall become remains unanswered. Will this new empire pursue military hegemony over the continent, or will it build an economic colossus that reshapes European commerce?

event.title: The German Question
event.text: The unification of Germany has settled one question but raised a greater one. A nation of such strength, population, and central position cannot simply exist; it must choose a direction. The armies that forged this state stand ready, and the factories that armed them hum with potential. What shall Germany become?

options.text: Germany shall find its destiny.

destiny.name: Wars of Unification
destiny.text: Secure the frontiers of the new German state by seizing the Baltic port of Danzig and the Lorraine fortress of Metz. Both are strategic linchpins, one commands the Vistula and access to the Baltic, the other guards the approaches from France.

conditions.text: Chose the Blood and Iron destiny
Own Gdańsk, or a subject owns it
Own Metz, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Wars of Unification
event.text: The cannons have spoken and the maps redrawn. German armies have marched east to the Vistula and west to the Moselle, seizing the fortresses and ports that secure the Reich's frontiers. The officer corps returns triumphant, forged in the fire of campaign into the finest military instrument in Europe. The great powers take notice, and begin to fear.

options.text: Our armies have proven their worth.

destiny.name: Elsass-Lothringen
destiny.text: Consolidate German military supremacy by securing Konigsberg in the east and raising an army of 50,000 that is the envy of Europe. The great powers must learn to respect German strength.

conditions.text: Own Königsberg, or a subject owns it

event.title: Elsass-Lothringen
event.text: The annexation of Lorraine and the consolidation of Prussia's Baltic territories marks Germany as the undisputed military power of Central Europe. Our fortresses bristle with artillery, our supply lines stretch from the North Sea to the Carpathians. The question now is doctrine, shall we perfect the art of siege warfare, reducing enemy strongholds with methodical precision? Or shall we embrace the war of movement, striking deep before the enemy can react?

options.text: Reduce their fortresses to rubble.

modifiers.name: Siege Mastery
modifiers.text: German artillery and siege engineers have perfected the systematic reduction of enemy fortifications, though the expense of prolonged siege operations strains the treasury.

options.text: Strike fast, before they know we are coming.

modifiers.name: Bewegungskrieg
modifiers.text: German doctrine emphasizes rapid decisive operations, strike before the enemy can concentrate, shatter their will, and dictate terms. Swift victories breed confidence, perhaps too much.

destiny.name: Mitteleuropa
destiny.text: Realize the dream of a German-led Central Europe by extending power over Warsaw and Krakow. Build the mightiest army on the continent in the age of the mass armies, and earn the prestige befitting a great empire. Unlocks the Krupp Stahlwerk.

conditions.text: Own Warsaw, or a subject owns it
Own Kraków, or a subject owns it

event.title: Mitteleuropa
event.text: German eagles fly over Warsaw and Krakow. The dream of Mitteleuropa, a continent organized under German leadership, has become reality. From the industrial Rhineland to the grain fields of Poland, from the Baltic ports to the Alpine passes, an empire of unprecedented power stretches across the heart of Europe. How shall this colossus comport itself among the nations?

options.text: Our strength will guarantee the peace.

modifiers.name: Armed Peace
modifiers.text: Germany's overwhelming military strength guarantees European order. No power dares challenge the Reich, and German prestige reaches its zenith as the arbiter of continental affairs.

options.text: The state exists to wage war.

modifiers.name: Total War
modifiers.text: The state is an instrument of war, and war is the instrument of the state. Germany's military machine mobilizes every resource for conquest, though the navy suffers from neglect.

destiny.name: Zollverein Expansion
destiny.text: Build the financial infrastructure and resource base to power German industry. Adopt Free Trade, so the tolls between the German lands fall as they fell in the Zollverein, fill the treasury, and ensure coal flows through the markets that fuel the factories of the future.

conditions.text: Chose the Legacy of the Zollverein destiny
A market the country is in

children.text: Coal is produced in the market
Coal is traded in the market

event.title: Handelsherrschaft
event.text: The Zollverein's vision has been realized. German banks extend credit from Frankfurt to Vienna, coal from the Ruhr powers factories across the customs union, and merchants who once haggled over petty tolls now command markets that span the German lands. The dismantling of internal barriers has created a unified economic space unlike anything Europe has seen, and the foundation for something greater.

options.text: The customs union is only the beginning.

destiny.name: Industriemacht
destiny.text: Transform Germany into an industrial powerhouse. Build Essen up from a village on a coal seam into a town of furnaces, and ensure steel production feeds the factories of the Ruhr and Rhine.

conditions.text: We own Essen and its development is at least 29
We own Essen and it has grown into a town or larger
A market the country is in

children.text: Steel is produced in the market
Steel is traded in the market

event.title: Industriemacht
event.text: The transformation is staggering. Where once there were scattered workshops and artisan guilds, now vast factory complexes line the rivers and railways of the German lands. Steel pours from the Ruhr furnaces, chemicals from the laboratories of the Rhine, machinery from the workshops of Saxony. German development has surged past its rivals. But how shall this industrial colossus organize its economy, through open competition or state direction?

options.text: Let the market decide. Free trade enriches all.

modifiers.name: Open Market
modifiers.text: Germany's open economic policies attract talent and capital from across Europe, integrating diverse peoples into a flourishing commercial union, though central authority loosens in the process.

options.text: The state must direct the economy's course.

modifiers.name: Directed Economy
modifiers.text: The state directs industrial development with Prussian efficiency, assimilating peoples and streamlining governance, though naval construction suffers as resources flow to factories.

destiny.name: Welthandel
destiny.text: Achieve economic supremacy over Europe. Amass vast wealth, earn worldwide prestige, open a Stock Exchange, and build Hamburg into the port through which German goods reach the world. Unlocks the Handelskammer.

conditions.text: We own Hamburg and its development is at least 58

event.title: Welthandel
event.text: German industry and German capital have reshaped the economy of a continent. From the counting houses of Hamburg to the bourses of Frankfurt, from the coal fields of the Ruhr to the laboratories of Berlin, Germany has become the workshop of Europe and the envy of the world. The sciences flourish in German universities, and German goods command premium prices in every market. The question is whether Germany's future lies on the waves of global commerce or in the factories that have already remade society.

options.text: Germany must command the seas of commerce.

modifiers.name: Handelsmacht
modifiers.text: Germany projects commercial power across the seas, building a maritime presence that rivals the old trading empires. The navy commands the shipping lanes, though land forces receive less attention.

options.text: The factory shall remake the world.

modifiers.name: Industriekaiser
modifiers.text: German industry and innovation reshape European society. The Reich's factories, laboratories, and universities lead the world, and all estates prosper under the engine of progress.

units.name: Schwarze Reiter
units.text: The Black Riders are heavily armored pistol cavalry who employ the caracole formation, riding forward in ranks to deliver pistol volleys before wheeling away to reload. Their blackened armor and thunderous volleys terrorize enemy formations.

units.name: Schützen
units.text: Picked marksmen with rifled pieces, drawn from the shooting guilds of the towns. They fight in open order ahead of the line and work round a flank, and their aimed fire kills at a range a musket cannot answer. A rifle is slow to load and carries no bayonet, so they lose men fast when caught in the open.

units.name: Kantonisten
units.text: Men enrolled from boyhood in the canton of their regiment. They drill with it for two months each spring and spend the rest of the year on their farms: steady under fire, slow into action.

units.name: Landwehr
units.text: The Landwehr are citizen-soldiers drawn from the general population, trained in basic military drill and armed by the state. What they lack in professional polish they make up for in numbers and patriotic determination.

units.name: Deutsche Feldartillerie
units.text: German field artillery batteries, benefiting from centuries of metallurgical expertise and systematic gunnery training, deliver devastating bombardments with exceptional accuracy and range.

buildings.name: Bergwerk
buildings.text: A German mining complex exploiting the rich mineral deposits of Central Europe. Skilled miners and engineers extract silver, copper, and iron using advanced techniques developed in the Harz and Erzgebirge. Sunk where the land itself yields silver, copper or iron.

children.text: The location's raw material is Silver
The location's raw material is Copper
The location's raw material is Iron

buildings.name: Rathaus
buildings.text: The civic town hall, seat of burgher self-governance and symbol of German civic pride. Here the city council meets, justice is administered, and the commercial life of the town is regulated.

buildings.name: Druckerei
buildings.text: A printing house following the tradition of Gutenberg, producing books, pamphlets, and scholarly works that spread knowledge and literacy across the German lands and beyond.

buildings.name: Waffenschmiede
buildings.text: A German arms foundry where master smiths forge weapons, armor, and firearms of renowned quality. The tradition of Solingen blades and Suhl muskets supplies armies across Europe.

buildings.name: Universitat
buildings.text: A German research university in the tradition of Heidelberg and Leipzig, where scholars advance knowledge through systematic inquiry and students receive a Bildung that shapes the mind as much as it fills it.

buildings.name: Krupp Stahlwerk
buildings.text: A massive steel works and armaments factory in the tradition of the Krupp dynasty. Here, mountains of Ruhr coal and iron are transmuted into the finest cannons and armor plate in the world, powering Germany's military-industrial dominance.

buildings.name: Handelskammer
buildings.text: A German chamber of commerce where merchants, bankers, and industrialists coordinate the economic affairs of the Reich. Trade agreements, market intelligence, and commercial disputes are managed with Prussian efficiency.

list.name: Reichskammergericht
list.text: The Imperial Chamber Court founded at the 1495 Diet of Worms as the price of the Ewiger Landfrieden: the eternal peace that abolished the right of feud. Sat at Frankfurt, then Speyer, then Wetzlar, with its judges chosen overwhelmingly by the Imperial Estates rather than the Emperor and its budget paid by the Empire itself. For three centuries it gave princes and free cities a credible legal forum against imperial overreach, anchoring the Reich's character as a constitutional, judicialised polity.

list.name: Reichshofrat
list.text: The Aulic Council, the Emperor's own supreme court at the Hofburg in Vienna, regulated by Ferdinand I in 1559 with a president, a vice-chancellor, and eighteen councillors all paid out of the imperial purse. It held exclusive jurisdiction over fiefs held directly of the Emperor and over matters of dynastic concern, and litigants flocked to it because it ruled faster than the Reichskammergericht and carried the Habsburg's personal authority. A direct counterweight to the estates' court at Wetzlar.

list.name: Reichskreise
list.text: The ten Imperial Circles created by Maximilian I from 1500 onward to organise common defence, collect imperial taxes, and (after 1512) enforce the verdicts of the Reichskammergericht. Each Kreis was led by two Kreisdirektoren, normally the senior secular and ecclesiastical princes, and its Kreistag mustered Reichsarmee contingents and regulated coinage. The Swabian and Franconian circles in particular gave imperial law real teeth in the territorially fractured south and west.

list.name: Sachsenspiegel
list.text: The Mirror of the Saxons, compiled in Middle Low German between 1220 and 1235 by the Saxon administrator Eike von Repgow at the request of Count Hoyer of Falkenstein. Its Landrecht (territorial law) and Lehnrecht (feudal law) became the template for the Schwabenspiegel, the Deutschenspiegel, and most local custumals across the German lands. Courts in parts of Saxony and Westphalia were still applying its provisions as late as 1900, a thicket of codified custom that bound princes as firmly as it bound peasants.

list.name: Hansetag and Kontore
list.text: The Hanseatic League's irregular general diet at Lubeck and its four great trading factories at the Steelyard in London, Bruges, Bergen, and Novgorod. Each Kontor was a chartered universitas mercatorum with its own treasury, seal, court, code of rules, and elected Aldermen, granting the Hanse cities a parallel commercial-legal order outside territorial princely jurisdiction. Even after the League's last formal Hansetag in 1669, the free cities of Lubeck, Hamburg and Bremen preserved their Hanseatic privileges into the 19th century.

list.name: Generaldirektorium
list.text: Frederick William I's General Directory, established by the Instructions of 20 December 1722 to merge the General Finance Directorate, the War Commissariat, and the Domains Administration into a single ministerial board with the Soldatenkonig as its president. Its four ministers split the kingdom by both province and function, audited the royal accounts daily, and made Brandenburg-Prussia the first European state where civil and military administration ran on the same disciplined fiscal cassettes, the foundation of Prussian power.

list.name: Zollverein
list.text: The German Customs Union concluded at Berlin on 22 March 1833 and entering force on 1 January 1834. The treaty abolished roughly 1,800 internal tariff barriers among the German states, consolidated more than thirty currencies into two, and drew 28 of the 39 members of the German Confederation into a Prussian-led free-trade zone. Austria alone refused to join, with fateful consequences. The Zollverein's railways, mints and uniform tariffs were the economic substrate on which political unification was achieved a generation later.
